title: Two Pointers: Merge Sorted Arrays & 3Sum

problems.title: Merge Sorted Array
problems.idea: Three-pointer merge from the end. Uses p1 at end of nums1, p2 at end of nums2, and p3 at very end. Merging from the end avoids overwriting unprocessed elements.
problems.description: You are given two sorted arrays nums1 (length m+n) and nums2 (length n). Merge nums2 into nums1 in-place in sorted order.
hints: Merge from the end to avoid overwriting elements. Three pointers: p1=m-1, p2=n-1, p3=m+n-1.

problems.title: 3Sum
problems.idea: Sort + two pointers. Fix i, use j and k to find pairs summing to -nums[i]. Skip duplicates at each pointer.
problems.description: Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j != k and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0. The solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.
hints: Fix one number, reduce to 2Sum on the rest.
Sort first to skip duplicates easily.
Use two pointers for the inner 2Sum loop.

title: Trees: Recursion & Validate Binary Search Tree

problems.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
problems.code:
class Solution:
    def isValidBST(self, root):
        self.prev = float('-inf')
        self.flag = True
        self.dfs(root)
        return self.flag

    def dfs(self, root):
        if not root: return
        self.dfs(root.left)
        if root.val <= self.prev: self.flag = False
        self.prev = root.val
        self.dfs(root.right)
problems.idea: In-order traversal must produce strictly increasing sequence. Track prev value with class variable. Any violation sets flag to False.
problems.description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST). A valid BST: left subtree has only keys < node's key; right subtree has only keys > node's key; both subtrees are also BSTs.

examples.explanation: Root is 5 but right child is 4.

hints: In-order traversal should produce strictly increasing values.
Pass min/max bounds recursively: left must be < node, right must be > node.

title: Dynamic Programming: Paint House

problems.title: Paint House
problems.idea: Bottom-up DP in-place. For each house i, update costs[i][color] by adding the min of the OTHER two colors from house i+1.
problems.description: There are n houses in a row, each can be painted red, blue, or green. Adjacent houses cannot have the same color. Given costs[i][j] (cost to paint house i with color j), return the minimum cost to paint all houses.
hints: DP: costs[i][0] += min(costs[i-1][1], costs[i-1][2]). Accumulate in-place from left to right.

title: Dynamic Programming: House Robber

problems.title: House Robber
problems.idea: Classic 1D DP. dp[i] = max money from houses 0..i. Recurrence: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]).
problems.description: You are a robber. Each house has money. You can't rob adjacent houses (triggers alarm). Return the maximum money you can rob.
hints: DP: rob[i] = max(rob[i-1], rob[i-2] + nums[i]). Only need previous two values.

title: Backtracking: Palindrome Partitioning & Word Search

problems.title: Palindrome Partitioning
problems.idea: Backtrack from pivot index. Try every substring — if palindrome, add to path and recurse from i+1. Pop on backtrack.
problems.description: Given a string s, partition s such that every substring of the partition is a palindrome. Return all possible palindrome partitionings.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.
hints: Backtrack: from current index, try every possible palindromic prefix and recurse on the suffix.

problems.title: Word Search
problems.idea: DFS backtracking. Mark visited cells as '#', recurse into 4 directions, restore on backtrack.
problems.description: Given an m×n grid of characters and a string word, return true if word exists in the grid. The word can be constructed from sequentially adjacent cells (horizontal/vertical). Each cell may not be used more than once.
hints: DFS from each cell. Mark visited cells temporarily. Backtrack if a path fails.

title: Trees & Linked List: Reverse LL, Cycle II & BT Max Path Sum

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.idea: Iterative pointer reversal: save next, point current to prev, advance both.
problems.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the reversed list.
hints: Iterative: prev=null, curr=head. Each step: next=curr.next, curr.next=prev, prev=curr, curr=next.
Recursive: reverse(head.next), then head.next.next=head, head.next=null.

problems.title: Linked List Cycle II
problems.idea: Floyd's algorithm. Phase 1: slow/fast meet inside cycle. Phase 2: reset slow to head — they meet at cycle entry.
problems.description: Given the head of a linked list, return the node where a cycle begins, or null if there is no cycle.
hints: Floyd's: fast+slow meet inside cycle. Reset slow to head, advance both one step at a time — they meet at the cycle start.

problems.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
problems.code:
class Solution:
    def maxPathSum(self, root):
        self.maxSum = root.val
        def dfs(node):
            if not node: return 0
            l = max(dfs(node.left), 0)
            r = max(dfs(node.right), 0)
            self.maxSum = max(self.maxSum, l+r+node.val)
            return max(l, r) + node.val
        dfs(root)
        return self.maxSum
problems.idea: Post-order DFS. Clamp child sums to 0, check arch sum vs global max, return max single branch + val.
problems.description: A path in a binary tree is a sequence of nodes where each adjacent pair is connected. Return the maximum path sum of any non-empty path (path doesn't need to go through root).
hints: Post-order DFS. At each node, max contribution upward = node.val + max(0, left, right). Max path through node = node.val + max(0,left) + max(0,right). Update global max.

title: Arrays & Two Pointers: Game of Life & Container With Most Water

problems.title: Game of Life
problems.idea: Two-pass in-place with encoding: -1 = alive→dead, 2 = dead→alive. Both 1 and -1 count as alive when checking neighbors.
problems.description: The Game of Life: given an m×n board of live (1) and dead (0) cells, apply all four rules simultaneously. Update the board to its next state in-place.
hints: Use extra states (2 = was alive, dies; 3 = was dead, becomes alive) to encode both old and new state simultaneously.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.idea: Two-pointer greedy. Always move the pointer with the shorter height — it is the bottleneck.
problems.description: Given an integer array `height` of length `n`, find two lines that form a container holding the most water. Return the maximum amount of water.
hints: O(n²) brute force works but is too slow.
Use two pointers at both ends. Move the pointer with the smaller height inward.
Area = min(height[l], height[r]) * (r - l).

title: Binary Search: Missing Number & First / Last Position

problems.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.idea: Compare mid with right. If nums[mid] > nums[right], min is in right half. Otherwise narrow to left.
problems.description: Given a sorted array rotated between 1 and n times, return the minimum element. Must run in O(log n).
hints: Binary search. If nums[mid] > nums[right], minimum is in right half. Otherwise in left half (including mid).

problems.title: Missing Number
problems.idea: Gauss formula: expected sum n*(n+1)/2 minus actual sum = missing number.
problems.description: Given an array nums containing n distinct numbers in range [0, n], return the only number in range missing from the array.
hints: Math: expected sum = n*(n+1)/2, subtract actual sum.
XOR: XOR all indices and all values — duplicates cancel, missing number remains.

problems.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
problems.idea: Two binary searches — one for leftmost (continue left on match), one for rightmost (continue right on match).
problems.description: Given a sorted array nums and a target, find the starting and ending position of target. If not found return [-1, -1]. Must be O(log n).
hints: Run two binary searches: one for leftmost occurrence, one for rightmost.

title: BFS: Rotten Oranges & Employee Importance

problems.title: Rotting Oranges
problems.idea: Multi-source BFS. Enqueue all initially rotten oranges. Each BFS level = 1 minute. Return -1 if fresh remain.
problems.description: Given an m×n grid where 0=empty, 1=fresh orange, 2=rotten orange, every minute fresh oranges 4-directionally adjacent to rotten ones become rotten. Return minimum minutes until no fresh orange remains, or -1 if impossible.
hints: Multi-source BFS from all rotten oranges simultaneously. Count fresh oranges. If any remain after BFS, return -1.

problems.title: Employee Importance
problems.idea: BFS with adjacency map id→[importance, subordinates]. Sum importance of all reachable employees.
problems.description: Each employee has an id, importance value, and list of direct subordinate IDs. Given an id, return the total importance of that employee plus all direct and indirect subordinates.
hints: BFS/DFS from the given employee. Accumulate importance values as you traverse the subordinate tree.

title: DP II: Longest Common Subsequence & Jump Game II

problems.title: Longest Common Subsequence
problems.idea: Bottom-up 2D DP from bottom-right to top-left. If chars match: dp[i][j]=dp[i+1][j+1]+1, else max of skipping either.
problems.description: Given two strings text1 and text2, return the length of their longest common subsequence. If none exists, return 0.
hints: DP: dp[i][j] = LCS of text1[0..i-1] and text2[0..j-1]. If chars match, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]+1. Otherwise max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

problems.title: Jump Game II
problems.idea: Greedy BFS-like. Maintain window [start, end]. Scan window for farthest reach, jump++, advance window.
problems.description: Given a 0-indexed array nums where each element is the max jump length from that index, return the minimum number of jumps to reach the last index.
constraints: It's guaranteed you can reach the last index.
hints: Greedy: track the farthest reachable index. Each time you exhaust the current jump range, increment jumps.

title: Hashing: Contiguous Array & Longest Palindrome

problems.title: Contiguous Array
problems.idea: Treat 0→-1, running sum. Same rSum at two indices means equal 0s and 1s between them. Init {0:-1}.
problems.description: Given a binary array nums, return the maximum length of a contiguous subarray with equal number of 0s and 1s.
hints: Replace 0s with -1, compute prefix sums. If the same prefix sum appears at index i and j, subarray [i+1..j] has equal 0s and 1s. Use a hash map to store first occurrence.

problems.title: Longest Palindrome
problems.idea: HashSet toggle: pair up chars (count+=2), add 1 for center if any unpaired char remains.
problems.description: Given a string s of lowercase and uppercase letters, return the length of the longest palindrome that can be built with those letters.
hints: Count character frequencies. All even-count chars can be used fully. One odd-count char can go in the middle. Sum = sum of all floors + 1 if any odd count exists.

title: Monotonic Stack: Daily Temperatures & Next Greater Element II

problems.title: Daily Temperatures
problems.idea: Monotonic decreasing stack of indices. For each temp, pop all smaller and set result[idx] = i - idx.
problems.description: Given array temperatures, return an array where answer[i] is the number of days until a warmer temperature. If no warmer future day, answer[i] = 0.
hints: Monotonic stack of indices. For each temperature, pop all smaller temperatures from stack and compute their wait days.

problems.title: Next Greater Element II
problems.idea: Iterate 2n times with i%n to simulate circular. Only push indices during first n.
problems.description: Given a circular integer array nums, return the next greater number for every element. If none exists, return -1.
hints: Monotonic stack. Iterate 2*n times (using mod). Push indices, pop when a larger element is found.

title: BFS: Binary Tree Level Order & Right Side View

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.idea: BFS with level tracking. Record queue size at start of each level, pop exactly that many nodes, enqueue children.
problems.description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (left to right, level by level).
hints: BFS with a queue. At each level, process all nodes in the current queue batch before adding their children.

problems.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
problems.idea: DFS left then right, tracking depth. Each depth value is overwritten until rightmost node sets it last.
problems.description: Given the root of a binary tree, imagine standing on the right side. Return values of nodes visible from the right side, top to bottom.
hints: BFS level order. Take the last node of each level. Or DFS right-first, record first node seen at each depth.

title: Design: Min Stack & HashMap with Chaining

problems.title: Min Stack
problems.idea: Two stacks: main and min-stack. Push to min-stack only when val ≤ current min. Pop both when tops match.
problems.description: Design a stack supporting push, pop, top, and getMin in O(1) time.
hints: Maintain a second stack that tracks the minimum at each level. Push min onto it when push is called, pop it when pop is called.

problems.title: Design HashMap
problems.idea: Separate chaining with 100 buckets and dummy head nodes. findPrev helper returns predecessor for O(1) insert/delete.
problems.description: Design a HashMap without built-in hash table libraries. Support put(key,value), get(key), and remove(key).

examples.input: put(1,1), put(2,2), get(1), get(3), put(2,1), get(2), remove(2), get(2)

hints: Array of linked lists (chaining) with (key, value) pairs. Same bucket approach as HashSet.

title: BFS: Cousins in BT, Symmetric Tree & N-ary Level Order

problems.title: Cousins in Binary Tree
problems.idea: BFS level-by-level. Check same level AND different parents (not children of same node).
problems.description: Two nodes are cousins if they have the same depth but different parents. Given the binary tree root and two node values x and y, return true if x and y are cousins.
constraints: x and y both exist in tree
hints: BFS level order. Check that x and y are at the same level but have different parents.

problems.title: Symmetric Tree
problems.idea: Recursive mirror check: left.val==right.val, left.left mirrors right.right, left.right mirrors right.left.
problems.description: Given the root of a binary tree, check whether it is a mirror of itself (symmetric around its center).
hints: Recursive: left.left mirrors right.right, left.right mirrors right.left.
Iterative: use a queue with pairs of nodes to compare.

problems.title: N-ary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.idea: Standard BFS — same as binary tree but enqueue all node.children.
problems.description: Given an n-ary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values.
hints: BFS with a queue. Process all nodes at each level, enqueue their children.

title: Tries: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)

problems.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
problems.idea: Array-based trie. Each node has children[26] and isEnd flag. Insert creates missing nodes. Search checks isEnd at path end.
problems.description: Implement a Trie (prefix tree) with insert, search, and startsWith operations.

examples.input: insert("apple"), search("apple"), search("app"), startsWith("app"), insert("app"), search("app")

hints: Each node has a dict of children and a is_end flag. insert walks/creates nodes. search walks and checks is_end. startsWith just walks.

title: Graph BFS/DFS: Course Schedule & All Nodes Distance K

problems.title: Course Schedule
problems.idea: Kahn's algorithm. Start with all indegree-0 nodes. Decrement neighbors. If all processed, no cycle.
problems.description: There are numCourses courses (0 to numCourses-1) and prerequisites [a,b] meaning you must take b before a. Return true if you can finish all courses.
hints: Equivalent to cycle detection in a directed graph. Use DFS with states: unvisited/visiting/visited. Cycle = impossible.

problems.title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree
problems.idea: Convert tree to undirected graph via BFS. Then DFS from target tracking depth — collect nodes at depth k.
problems.description: Given a binary tree, a target node value, and integer k, return all node values that are exactly k distance from the target node.
hints: Build a parent map (to traverse upward). Then BFS from target node in all 3 directions (left child, right child, parent) for k steps.

title: Sliding Window: Longest Substring & Find All Anagrams

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.idea: Sliding window with hash set. Shrink from left when duplicate found. Each char added/removed at most once.
problems.description: Given a string `s`, find the length of the longest substring without duplicate characters.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.
hints: Use a sliding window. Expand right pointer, shrink left when a duplicate is found.
Track characters in a set or hash map for O(1) lookup.

problems.title: Find All Anagrams in a String
problems.idea: Fixed-size sliding window with Counter comparison. Slide by adding right char and removing left char.
problems.description: Given strings s and p, return all start indices of p's anagrams in s.
hints: Sliding window of size len(p). Compare character frequency arrays. Slide and update counts.

title: Backtracking: Subsets

problems.title: Subsets
problems.idea: Iterative cascading: start with [[]], for each num copy all existing subsets, append num, add to result.
problems.description: Given an integer array nums of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set). The solution must not contain duplicate subsets.
hints: Backtrack: at each index decide to include or exclude. Or iteratively add each number to all existing subsets.

title: BFS/Graph: Word Ladder, 01 Matrix & Flood Fill

problems.title: Word Ladder
problems.idea: BFS + wildcard adjacency list. Pre-build pattern→words map. BFS through patterns to find shortest transformation.
problems.description: Given beginWord, endWord and wordList, return the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord where each step changes exactly one letter and every intermediate word is in wordList. Return 0 if no sequence exists.
hints: BFS from beginWord. For each word, try changing every character (a-z). If the new word is in wordList, add to queue and remove from set.

problems.title: 01 Matrix
problems.idea: Multi-source BFS from all 0s. Mark 1-cells as -1, process level by level assigning increasing distance.
problems.description: Given an m×n binary matrix mat, return the distance of the nearest 0 for each cell.
hints: Multi-source BFS: start from all 0s simultaneously. Distance to each cell is its BFS level.

problems.title: Flood Fill
problems.idea: Recursive DFS. Color change acts as visited marker. Guard: return early if new color = original.
problems.description: Given an image (m×n grid), perform a flood fill starting from pixel (sr,sc): change its color to `color` and recursively change all 4-directionally adjacent pixels of the same original color.
hints: DFS/BFS from (sr,sc). Only change cells matching the original color. Handle the edge case where starting color equals new color.

title: Trees: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers & Path Sum II

problems.title: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers
problems.idea: DFS accumulating number: currSum = currSum*10 + val. At leaf nodes add to total.
problems.description: Given the root of a binary tree with digits 0-9, where each root-to-leaf path represents a number, return the total sum of all root-to-leaf numbers.
hints: DFS passing current accumulated number. At leaf, add to total. current = current * 10 + node.val.

problems.title: Path Sum II
problems.idea: DFS backtracking with path list. Append on enter, pop on exit. At leaf if sum matches, copy path.
problems.description: Given the root of a binary tree and targetSum, return all root-to-leaf paths where the sum of node values equals targetSum.
hints: DFS + backtracking. Add node to path, subtract from remaining sum. At leaf, check if remaining == 0.

title: Heaps & DP: Top K Frequent, Unique Paths & Minimum Path Sum

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.idea: Bucket sort: bucket[freq] = elements. Iterate from highest freq down collecting k elements. O(n) vs O(n log k) heap.
problems.description: Given integer array nums and integer k, return the k most frequent elements. Answer is guaranteed to be unique.
constraints: k is in range [1, unique element count]
hints: Count frequencies, then use a min-heap of size k. Or bucket sort by frequency (O(n)).

problems.title: Unique Paths
problems.idea: Space-optimized 1D DP. Right-to-left each row: dp[i] += dp[i+1]. Repeat m-1 times.
problems.description: A robot on an m×n grid starts at top-left and moves only right or down. Return the number of unique paths to reach bottom-right.
hints: DP: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]. First row and column are all 1s.

problems.title: Minimum Path Sum
problems.idea: Bottom-up DP in-place. Fill last col then row, then inner: grid[r][c] += min(right, down).
problems.description: Given an m×n grid of non-negative numbers, find a path from top-left to bottom-right (only right or down) that minimizes the sum of all numbers along the path.
hints: DP in-place: grid[i][j] += min(grid[i-1][j], grid[i][j-1]).

title: Two Pointers: 2Sum, Sort Colors & Remove Duplicates

problems.title: Two Sum
problems.idea: Single-pass hashmap. For each element compute complement. If complement in map, return pair.
problems.description: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`. You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
hints: A brute force approach checks all pairs — O(n²). Can you do better?
Fix one number x, search for target-x. Can you make that search faster?
Use a hash map to store seen values and look up target-x in O(1).

problems.title: Sort Colors
problems.idea: Count occurrences of 0, 1, 2. Overwrite array. Alternatively, Dutch National Flag for single pass.
problems.description: Given an array nums with n objects colored red (0), white (1), or blue (2), sort them in-place in that order without using the library sort function.
hints: Dutch National Flag algorithm: three pointers low, mid, high. Swap 0s to front, 2s to back.

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
problems.idea: Slow pointer writes unique values. When fast finds new value, slow advances and copies.
problems.description: Given a sorted integer array nums in non-decreasing order, remove duplicates in-place so each unique element appears only once. Return the number of unique elements k.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.
hints: Two pointers: slow tracks last unique position, fast scans forward.
When nums[fast] != nums[slow], increment slow and copy.

title: Linked List: Intersection, Reorder & Remove Nth Node

problems.title: Intersection of Two Linked Lists
problems.idea: Two pointers: when one hits null redirect to other's head. They meet at intersection after traversing a+b+c total.
problems.description: Given heads of two singly linked lists, return the node where they intersect. Return null if no intersection. Lists must retain original structure after.
hints: Two pointers: when one reaches end, redirect to other list's head. They meet at intersection after at most m+n steps.

problems.title: Reorder List
problems.idea: Three steps: find middle, reverse second half, merge two halves alternating.
problems.description: Reorder a singly linked list L0→L1→…→Ln-1→Ln to L0→Ln→L1→Ln-1→L2→Ln-2→…. Do not modify node values.
hints: Find mid with slow/fast. Reverse the second half. Merge both halves alternately.

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
problems.code:
class Solution:
    def removeNthFromEnd(self, head, n):
        dummy=ListNode(0,head); slow=fast=dummy
        for _ in range(n+1): fast=fast.next
        while fast: slow,fast=slow.next,fast.next
        slow.next=slow.next.next
        return dummy.next
problems.idea: Dummy node + gap of n+1. Move fast n+1 steps, then both until fast is null. Skip slow.next.
problems.description: Given the head of a linked list, remove the nth node from the end of the list and return its head.
hints: Use two pointers. Advance the fast pointer n steps ahead, then move both until fast reaches the end.

title: Backtracking: N-Queens

problems.title: N-Queens
problems.idea: Row-by-row backtracking. Track columns, diagonals (r-c) and anti-diagonals (r+c) with sets for O(1) safety checks.
problems.description: The n-queens puzzle: place n queens on an n×n chessboard so no two queens attack each other. Return all distinct solutions.
hints: Backtrack row by row. Track used columns and diagonals to prune invalid placements.

title: Design: Queue using Stacks & HashSet

problems.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
problems.idea: Two stacks. Transfer inStack→outStack lazily when outStack empty. Amortized O(1) per op.
problems.description: Implement a FIFO queue using only two stacks. Support push, pop, peek, and empty operations.
constraints: All calls to pop and peek are valid
hints: Two stacks: inbox and outbox. Push to inbox. For pop/peek, if outbox empty, pour inbox into outbox (reversing order). Amortized O(1).

problems.title: Design HashSet
problems.idea: Double hashing with 1000 buckets. primary[key%1000][key//1000] = bool. Lazily allocated per bucket.
problems.description: Design a HashSet without using built-in hash table libraries. Support add(key), contains(key), and remove(key).

examples.input: add(1), add(2), contains(1), contains(3), remove(2), contains(2)

hints: Array of linked lists (chaining). Hash = key % bucket_size. Handle collisions within each bucket.

title: Arrays: Find Disappeared Numbers

problems.title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
problems.idea: Negation marking. For each num negate nums[|num|-1]. Indices still positive = missing numbers.
problems.description: Given array nums of n integers where nums[i] is in [1,n], return all integers in [1,n] that do not appear in nums.
hints: Mark visited: negate nums[nums[i]-1]. Then collect all indices with positive values (0-indexed, add 1).

title: DP: Delete and Earn

problems.title: Delete and Earn
problems.idea: Transform to House Robber. freq[x] = x * count(x). Choosing x deletes x±1, reducing to non-adjacent max sum.
problems.description: Given integer array nums, each operation: pick nums[i], earn nums[i] points, delete all elements equal to nums[i]-1 and nums[i]+1. Maximize total points.
hints: Reduce to House Robber: bucket[v] = v * count(v). You can't take adjacent buckets. dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + bucket[i]).

title: Arrays: Diagonal Traverse & Spiral Matrix

problems.title: Diagonal Traverse
problems.idea: Simulation with flag. 1=up-right, -1=down-left. Change direction at boundaries.
problems.description: Given an m×n matrix mat, return all elements in diagonal order (alternating up-right and down-left diagonals).
hints: Track current direction. When going up-right, if hit top or right edge, switch to down-left. Adjust row/col boundaries accordingly.

problems.title: Spiral Matrix
problems.idea: Shrink 4 boundaries: take top row, right col, bottom row reversed, left col reversed. Repeat.
problems.description: Given an m×n matrix, return all elements in spiral order.
hints: Maintain four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right). Traverse each boundary, then shrink inward.

title: Binary Search: Search 2D Matrix & Rotated Sorted Array

problems.title: Search a 2D Matrix
problems.idea: Treat 2D matrix as flat sorted array. Map mid → matrix[mid//n][mid%n].
problems.description: Given an m×n integer matrix where each row is sorted and the first integer of each row is greater than the last of the previous row, return true if target is in the matrix. Must be O(log(m*n)).
hints: Treat the matrix as a flattened sorted array. Binary search on indices 0..m*n-1, convert mid to row/col with divmod.

problems.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.idea: Identify sorted half: if nums[lo]<=nums[mid] left is sorted. Check if target in that half; else go to other.
problems.description: There is an integer array nums sorted in ascending order (with distinct values), possibly rotated at unknown index k. Given nums after rotation and a target, return the index of target, or -1 if not found. Must be O(log n).
hints: One half is always sorted. Check which half and decide where target lies.

title: Hashing: Group Anagrams, Isomorphic Strings & Subarray Sum K

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.idea: Sort each string as canonical key. Group by sorted string in hashmap.
problems.description: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. Return the grouped anagrams in any order.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: Canonical form: sort each string's characters. Strings with the same sorted form are anagrams.

problems.title: Isomorphic Strings
problems.idea: Two hashmaps: s→t and t→s. Each char must map bidirectionally to exactly one char.
problems.description: Two strings s and t are isomorphic if characters in s can be replaced to get t. All occurrences must be replaced consistently; no two characters may map to the same character.
hints: Maintain two maps: s→t and t→s. If a character is seen before with a different mapping, return false.

problems.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
problems.idea: Prefix sum hashmap {sum: count}. count += map[rSum - k]. Init {0:1}.
problems.description: Given integer array nums and integer k, return the total number of subarrays whose sum equals k.
hints: Prefix sum + hash map. If prefix[j] - prefix[i] = k, then subarray [i+1..j] sums to k. Store prefix sum counts.

title: Heaps: Kth Largest, Merge K Sorted Lists & Meeting Rooms II

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problems.idea: Min-heap of size k. After all insertions, heap top is the kth largest element.
problems.description: Given an integer array nums and integer k, return the kth largest element in the array (not kth distinct).
hints: Min-heap of size k: push elements, pop when size exceeds k. Top of heap is answer.
QuickSelect: partition and recurse on correct side. Average O(n).

problems.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
problems.idea: Min-heap of (val, idx). Pop minimum, append to result, push next from that list.
problems.description: You are given an array of k linked-lists, each sorted in ascending order. Merge all linked-lists into one sorted linked-list and return it.
hints: Use a min-heap (priority queue) of size k.
Or divide and conquer: merge pairs of lists repeatedly.

problems.title: Meeting Rooms II
problems.idea: Sort by start. Min-heap of end times. Reuse room if earliest end ≤ current start. Heap size = answer.
problems.description: Given an array of meeting time intervals [start, end], return the minimum number of conference rooms required.
hints: Sort by start time. Use a min-heap of end times. If earliest ending room is free (end <= current start), reuse it; otherwise add a new room.

title: Binary Search: Peak Element & More

problems.title: Find Peak Element
problems.idea: If nums[mid] < nums[mid+1], peak is in right half. Else peak is at mid or left. Converges to a peak.
problems.description: A peak element is strictly greater than its neighbors. Given nums, return the index of any peak element. Must be O(log n).
hints: Binary search: if nums[mid] < nums[mid+1], peak is on right. Otherwise on left (including mid).

title: Backtracking: Combination Sum

problems.title: Combination Sum
problems.idea: Backtracking from current index (reuse allowed). Sort and prune when candidate > remaining.
problems.description: Given an array of distinct integers candidates and a target integer, return all unique combinations where chosen numbers sum to target. The same number may be used unlimited times.
hints: Backtrack: at each step pick a candidate (or skip it). Allow reuse by not incrementing start index.

title: DP: Minimum Falling Path Sum & Product Except Self

problems.title: Minimum Falling Path Sum
problems.idea: Bottom-up DP in-place. Each cell += min of 2-3 cells directly below. Answer = min of top row.
problems.description: Given n×n matrix, return the minimum sum of any falling path through it. A falling path starts at any element in row 0 and at each step moves to the row below (directly below or one diagonal step left/right).
hints: DP in-place. matrix[i][j] += min(matrix[i-1][j-1], matrix[i-1][j], matrix[i-1][j+1]) (clamping at edges). Answer is min of last row.

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.code:
class Solution:
    def productExceptSelf(self, nums):
        n=len(nums); res=[1]*n
        for i in range(1,n): res[i]=res[i-1]*nums[i-1]
        r=1
        for i in range(n-1,-1,-1): res[i]*=r; r*=nums[i]
        return res
problems.idea: Two passes: left products in result array, then multiply by running right product in reverse.
problems.description: Given integer array nums, return an array where answer[i] is the product of all elements except nums[i]. Must run in O(n) without division.
hints: Two passes: first build prefix products, then suffix products. answer[i] = prefix[i] * suffix[i].

title: Graph: Town Judge, Number of Islands & Critical Connections

problems.title: Find the Town Judge
problems.idea: Net score: score += 1 for being trusted, -= 1 for trusting. Judge has score = n-1.
problems.description: In a town of n people (1..n), the town judge trusts nobody and everybody else trusts the judge. Given trust pairs [a,b], return the judge's label or -1.
hints: Track in-degree and out-degree. Judge has in-degree = n-1 and out-degree = 0.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.idea: DFS from each '1'. Mark as '0' to avoid revisiting. Each DFS call = one island.
problems.description: Given an m×n binary grid of '1's (land) and '0's (water), return the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and connected horizontally/vertically.
hints: DFS/BFS from each unvisited '1'. Mark visited cells as '0' (or seen). Count how many times you start a new DFS.

problems.title: Critical Connections in a Network
problems.idea: Tarjan's bridge algorithm. Track arrival and lowest reachable times. If lowest[child] > arrival[node], edge is a bridge.
problems.description: Given n servers and connections between them, a critical connection is one whose removal disconnects some servers. Return all critical connections.
hints: Tarjan's bridge-finding algorithm. Track discovery time and low value. Edge (u,v) is a bridge if low[v] > disc[u].

title: Trees: Balanced Binary Tree

problems.title: Balanced Binary Tree
problems.idea: Bottom-up height. Return -1 to signal imbalance early. Final check: height != -1.
problems.description: Given a binary tree, determine if it is height-balanced (the depth of the two subtrees of every node differs by at most 1).
hints: DFS returning height. If any subtree is unbalanced, propagate -1 upward to short-circuit.

title: DP: Coin Change

problems.title: Coin Change
problems.idea: 1D DP. dp[i] = min coins for amount i. For each coin: dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-coin]+1). Init to amount+1.
problems.description: Given an integer array coins of denominations and an integer amount, return the fewest coins needed to make that amount. Return -1 if impossible.
hints: Bottom-up DP: dp[i] = min coins to make amount i. dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-coin]+1) for each coin.

title: Tarjan's Algorithm Deep Dive: Critical Connections

problems.title: Critical Connections in a Network
problems.idea: Deep dive: Tarjan's bridge algorithm. low[child] > arrival[parent] means no back edge from child's subtree to parent or above — the edge is a bridge.
problems.description: Given n servers and connections between them, a critical connection is one whose removal disconnects some servers. Return all critical connections.
hints: Tarjan's bridge-finding algorithm. Track discovery time and low value. Edge (u,v) is a bridge if low[v] > disc[u].
